scope: Conservative receipt TTL bound: semantic soundness and per-call traversal complexity only
review: new independent finite adversarial review; no previous verdict supplied or consulted

independence.description: Fresh reviewer context, separate from builder, no builder reports or prior judgments. No descendants or additional critic were launched.

initialIndependentHarness.disposition: Two reproduced test-harness defects corrected in output only; first results retained. See harness-corrections.json.

accounting.passedTotal: 151 = 121 + 25 + 5; skipped journal cases do not count as PASS
accounting.journalSkipCause: Explicit -t scope selection, not a PostgreSQL availability result. PG was not used or probed under packet authority.

observations: The TTL skip is O(1) with respect to retained receipt cardinality; each necessary prune traverses all N retained deliveries including matched entries, so O(N).
Repeated expiration/backdating can cause O(K*N) TTL work. Store validation still copies maps; capacity/authority/reconciliation/projection have separate costs. No whole-store/global linearity claim.

limitations: Network/socket, provider, PostgreSQL, installation and descendant/process tests were not run under this authority.
Existing network-dependent 1000ms/<1300ms latency tests were preserved rather than weakened or substituted; default 15000ms unchanged.
Fsync fault injection after LF proves projection isolation and ambiguous complete-transaction replay; it is not an OS power-loss or child crash test.
Seeded finite tests plus integer-domain argument do not claim exhaustive execution of every Date input string.
preparationAndHarnessCorrections: Preserved preparation/test-harness defects corrected in output do not automatically invalidate the scoped review; acceptance rests on corrected discriminating evidence, unchanged source/original, Node22 and output-only execution. No additional tests repeated after evidence completed.
